provisioning_policy.intent: Provisioning must keep default scopes narrow, treat consent restrictions as first-class policy, and separate setup-time Google Cloud automation from runtime connector credentials.
provisioning_policy.default_scope_posture: Start with the least-broad scope set that supports the selected workflow; widen only on explicit feature selection or a method-level requirement that cannot be satisfied otherwise.
consent_restriction_rules: Do not request broad Gmail or Calendar scopes up front when a narrower read-only or event-scoped path satisfies the selected workflow.
Treat restricted Gmail scopes, broad Calendar scopes, and Chat app-auth scopes as explicit escalation points that the provisioning UX must explain before consent.

Google Workspace Events inherits scopes from the underlying product/event type, so setup must derive scopes from the selected event surface instead of inventing a separate broad workspaceevents scope.
runtime_separation_rules: Application Default Credentials, local credentials files, and gcloud-authenticated setup are provisioning-only inputs; runtime connectors must materialize credential_id handles or in-memory access tokens instead.
Provisioning must never persist client-secret JSON, refresh tokens, or credentials-file paths into connector-owned runtime configuration.
Any setup path that cannot produce a runtime-safe auth reference stops at provisioning completion and must not mark the connector runtime as ready.

automatable_steps: Select and verify the target Google Cloud project before enabling APIs or creating downstream resources.
Enable required Google APIs and Pub/Sub resources where doing so only changes project bootstrap state.
Create Pub/Sub topics/subscriptions and bind publisher IAM for Workspace Events delivery when the operator has the required project permissions.
Run non-secret diagnostics such as current project, enabled services, and Pub/Sub test pulls.
forbidden_steps: Silently broaden OAuth scopes or auto-approve escalation without an explicit operator choice.
Attempt to bypass OAuth consent, restricted-scope verification, Google Workspace admin approval, or organization policy gates.
Treat gcloud Application Default Credentials or local credential files as steady-state connector runtime auth.
Persist setup-time secrets or downloaded credential material into connector-owned state.
fallback_policy: If gcloud is unavailable or blocked, emit deterministic manual setup steps for the same project resources instead of relaxing policy.
Manual fallback must preserve the same default scope plan and escalation rules as the gcloud-assisted path.
Workspace Events provisioning must not create the upstream subscription until the Pub/Sub topic and publisher IAM prerequisites are confirmed.

project_prerequisites: OAuth consent screen configured for the selected project.
OAuth client created for the user-auth flow used by the host provisioning UX.

escalation_paths.trigger: User enables outbound send or draft-send workflows.
notes: Prefer send/compose over full mailbox scopes when composed delivery is the only added behavior.

escalation_paths.trigger: User enables message mutation workflows such as modify or trash.
notes: Trash/modify should not escalate directly to full mailbox access.

escalation_paths.trigger: User explicitly enables permanent delete or import-style full-mailbox operations.
notes: Restricted broad mailbox scope; require explicit acknowledgement that the workflow really needs irreversible or full-mailbox semantics.

escalation_paths.trigger: User enables settings, forwarding, or filter-management workflows.
notes: Forwarding and filter changes materially affect data routing and remain outside the default path.

gcloud_assisted_steps: Confirm Gmail API enablement for the chosen project before launching user consent.
Inspect current consent-screen/project posture so the setup UX can explain when requested scopes increase verification burden.
Use gcloud-authenticated setup only for project/bootstrap checks; final runtime output must still be a credential_id or in-memory token path.
fallback_steps: Provide manual console steps to enable the Gmail API and select or create the OAuth client when gcloud is unavailable.
Complete consent through the host provisioning flow, then materialize a runtime-safe credential reference instead of storing credential files.
runtime_materialization: Connector runtime accepts credential_id, in-memory access token, or refresh-token exchange via the shared Google auth substrate.
Credentials files, default credentials, and ADC remain provisioning-only and must not be passed through as runtime config.
notes: The initial Gmail migration target is the current read/list/history connector surface, so the default bundle stays on gmail.readonly until send or mutation features are explicitly selected.
History sync still depends on service-owned cursor/lease state, but that does not require scope widening beyond the read-only baseline.

project_prerequisites: OAuth consent screen configured for the selected project.
OAuth client created for the interactive Calendar user-auth flow.

escalation_paths.trigger: User enables event create, update, delete, or quick-add workflows.
notes: Prefer event-scoped mutation access over broader calendar-management scopes.

escalation_paths.trigger: User needs to create or manage secondary calendars owned by the app.
notes: Use the app-created scope before asking for full calendar ownership.

escalation_paths.trigger: User enables calendar-list mutation, calendar-property mutation, or ACL-management workflows.
notes: This is the broad/admin edge of Calendar provisioning and should be an explicit opt-in.

gcloud_assisted_steps: Confirm Calendar API enablement before launching user consent.
Preflight whether the requested feature set can stay on read-only or event-scoped permissions before requesting broader calendar management.
fallback_steps: Provide manual console steps for Calendar API enablement and OAuth client selection when gcloud cannot manage the project.
Keep the same default scope plan and return a runtime-safe credential reference after consent completes.
runtime_materialization: Runtime should use credential_id handles or ephemeral access tokens from the shared auth chain, never raw local credentials files.
Provisioning-only auth sources such as ADC may assist setup diagnostics but must not define steady-state connector auth.
notes: The current handwritten Calendar connector already separates runtime auth from setup by accepting token or credential_id only; migration should preserve that runtime shape while moving setup logic into the shared substrate.

project_prerequisites: OAuth consent screen configured for the selected project.
OAuth client created for the interactive Google Meet user-auth flow.
The selected account is allowed to use the requested Google Meet API preview or restricted surfaces.

escalation_paths.trigger: User enables Google Meet space creation workflows.
notes: Space creation is a write path and must stay separate from read-only space and conference artifact access.

escalation_paths.trigger: User enables Google Meet active-conference termination workflows.
notes: Ending an active conference is operationally disruptive and should be policy-gated by the connector operation.

escalation_paths.trigger: User enables Google Meet space settings read or patch workflows.
notes: Space settings expose or mutate meeting policy and should not be bundled into default artifact reads.

escalation_paths.trigger: User enables Google Meet Drive-backed transcript or smart-note text export.
notes: Drive-backed Meet artifacts require a distinct Drive scope and must be surfaced as a separate escalation.

gcloud_assisted_steps: Confirm Google Meet API enablement before launching user consent.
Preflight whether the selected workflow can stay on meetings.space.readonly before requesting creation, settings, or Drive-backed artifact scopes.
Use gcloud-authenticated setup only for project/bootstrap checks; final runtime output must still be a credential_id or in-memory token path.
fallback_steps: Provide manual console steps for Google Meet API enablement and OAuth client selection when gcloud cannot manage the project.
Keep space creation, conference termination, settings, and Drive-backed artifact scopes as explicit opt-ins in the manual fallback path.
Do not mark runtime readiness until the host has materialized a runtime-safe credential reference or ephemeral access token.
runtime_materialization: Runtime should use credential_id handles or ephemeral access tokens from the shared Google auth chain, never raw local credentials files.
Provisioning-only auth sources such as ADC may assist setup diagnostics but must not define steady-state connector auth.
Developer-preview or restricted-scope denial should be surfaced as structured doctor/self_check guidance instead of silently widening scopes.
notes: Google Meet is intentionally separate from Google Calendar hangoutLink preservation and Workspace Events delivery because its API owns spaces, conference records, participants, transcripts, recordings, smart notes, and active-conference lifecycle.
Live meeting participation, speech, and browser-control behavior is not part of the default API-artifact foundation and requires separate higher-risk capabilities.

project_prerequisites: OAuth consent screen configured for the selected project.
OAuth client created for the People user-auth flow used by the host provisioning UX.

escalation_paths.trigger: User enables contact create, update, photo update, or group-membership mutation workflows.
notes: Contact mutation requires the broad contacts scope; do not hide this behind read-only flows.

escalation_paths.trigger: User enables reads from Google-suggested other contacts.
notes: Other Contacts is a distinct personal-data surface and should be an explicit opt-in above ordinary contact reads.

escalation_paths.trigger: User enables Google Workspace directory search or lookup workflows.
notes: Directory reads expose org-wide profile data and should remain separate from personal contact access.

gcloud_assisted_steps: Confirm People API enablement before launching user consent.
Preflight whether the requested workflow can stay on contacts.readonly before adding contact mutation or directory scopes.
fallback_steps: Provide manual console steps for People API enablement and OAuth client selection when gcloud cannot manage the project.
Keep personal-contact, other-contacts, and directory scope choices explicit in the manual fallback path.
runtime_materialization: Runtime should use credential_id handles or ephemeral access tokens from the shared Google auth chain, never raw local credentials files.
Provisioning-only auth sources such as ADC may assist setup diagnostics but must not define steady-state connector auth.
notes: People/Contacts reads are privacy-sensitive even when they are non-mutating, so the connector should expose field-mask and source choices explicitly rather than widening by convenience wrapper.
Self-profile (`people/me`) access can require additional personal-profile scopes and is intentionally not part of the default contact-read path.

surfaces.display_name: Google Workspace Admin Reports connector provisioning
project_prerequisites: OAuth consent screen configured for the selected project or delegated Workspace-admin auth path.
A Google Workspace domain administrator or approved delegated-admin credential path exists for the selected tenant.
The selected tenant permits the requested Admin Reports restricted scopes.

escalation_paths.trigger: User enables usage-report workflows (user, customer, or entity usage metrics).
notes: Usage telemetry is a separate restricted admin surface and should not be silently bundled into audit-log access.

gcloud_assisted_steps: Confirm Admin SDK API enablement for the selected project before launching consent.
Validate that the selected account or delegated credential path actually has Workspace admin access for the target tenant.
Preflight whether the requested workflow can stay on audit.readonly or needs the separate usage.readonly scope.
fallback_steps: Provide manual console steps for Admin SDK API enablement and admin-approved OAuth client selection when gcloud cannot manage the project.
Do not mark runtime readiness until domain-admin consent or delegated credential materialization succeeds for the selected tenant.
runtime_materialization: Runtime should use credential_id handles or ephemeral access tokens from the shared Google auth chain; domain-wide delegated service-account material remains a host/provisioning concern.
Provisioning-only auth sources such as ADC may assist diagnostics but must not silently become steady-state runtime auth for admin connectors.
notes: Admin Reports is a domain-admin surface, not an end-user personal-data connector; setup must make tenant and admin assumptions explicit.
Audit and usage scopes should stay separately explainable because many environments will permit one but not the other.

project_prerequisites: Pub/Sub topic created in the same Google Cloud project used for the Workspace Events subscription.
Publisher IAM granted to the Google Workspace delivery service account for the selected event source.

escalation_paths.trigger: User selects Chat membership events instead of message-only events.
notes: Prefer readonly membership access unless mutation/admin behavior is explicitly requested.

escalation_paths.trigger: User selects Chat space metadata events.
notes: Keep the default user-auth flow on readonly scopes whenever possible.

escalation_paths.trigger: User enables Chat app-auth or higher-privilege event delivery paths that require administrator approval.
notes: App-auth Chat scopes stay out of the default path because they require separate admin and Chat app setup.

gcloud_assisted_steps: Enable the Google Workspace Events API and Pub/Sub API for the chosen project.
Create the Pub/Sub topic and pull subscription used as the notification endpoint.
Bind roles/pubsub.publisher on the topic to the correct Google Workspace delivery service account for the selected event source.
Run non-destructive test pulls from the Pub/Sub subscription after subscription creation.
fallback_steps: Provide exact manual console steps for API enablement, topic creation, publisher IAM, and pull-subscription creation when gcloud is unavailable.
Do not create the Workspace Events subscription until the Pub/Sub topic and IAM prerequisites are confirmed.
runtime_materialization: Workspace Events runtime receives normalized topic/subscription identifiers and a runtime-safe credential reference; Pub/Sub bootstrap credentials remain a provisioning concern.
Provisioning may test Pub/Sub delivery, but ongoing subscription renewal and delivery repair belong in the connector or host runtime.
notes: The default onboarding path assumes Chat message events because that keeps the first consent surface narrow; additional Workspace products can add their own explicit escalation entries later.
Workspace Events scopes come from the underlying Google Workspace product and event type, not from a separate broad workspaceevents OAuth scope.

helper_overlay_policy.intent: Handwritten helpers are allowed only as thin workflow overlays above generated Google operations.
require_all: Workflow spans multiple generated operations with ordered state transitions or compensating behavior.
Workflow needs connector-owned state/lease/cursor semantics not representable by one generated operation call.
Overlay adds explicit safety controls beyond per-operation policy (for example approval, dry-run, or budget gates).
Each helper step maps to concrete generated operation IDs and existing capability checks.
forbidden_patterns: Wrapping single generated operations as custom helpers without additional workflow semantics.
Adding hidden capabilities/scopes outside the generated policy mapping.
Embedding bespoke auth transport logic that belongs in the shared Google auth/executor substrate.
review_checklist: Document the generated operation sequence and compensation behavior.
Document replay/idempotency strategy for partial failures.
Document additional approval/budget/safety controls and owning policy object.
Add deterministic tests proving the helper remains a thin overlay.

initial_workflow_shortlist.summary: Incremental mailbox synchronization with checkpoint/lease fencing and history gap recovery.
safety_constraints: Monotonic history checkpoint updates with anti-regression guard.
Lease-aware execution so only one active sync writer advances cursor state.
rationale: Gmail history sync needs durable cursor semantics that are not captured by individual generated operations.

initial_workflow_shortlist.summary: Thread triage that fetches context, drafts response content, and sends with explicit recipient safeguards.
safety_constraints: Human-visible draft/summary checkpoint before the send step.
rationale: Composed read->write flow requires explicit sequencing and policy controls around outgoing email.

initial_workflow_shortlist.summary: Find available meeting windows then create an event with participant and recurrence constraints.
safety_constraints: Do not schedule outside policy-defined working windows/timezones.
Prevent duplicate event creation with idempotency keys or existing-event checks.
rationale: Scheduling is inherently multi-step and requires deterministic conflict checks plus write gating.

initial_workflow_shortlist.summary: Reschedule existing calendar events with attendee-impact awareness and bounded update fields.
safety_constraints: Only allow approved mutable fields for patch operations.
Require explicit confirmation when attendee list or meeting location changes.
rationale: Event updates require contextual read-before-write validation to avoid destructive meeting churn.

initial_workflow_shortlist.summary: Run analytic query jobs only after cost/allowlist preflight and store bounded result metadata.
safety_constraints: Enforce project/dataset allowlists before query execution.
Block or require approval when estimated bytes billed exceed policy budget.
rationale: BigQuery query execution has multi-step lifecycle and cost risk that needs explicit workflow-level controls.

exceptions: jobs.query can produce high data-scan costs and broad data exfiltration if project/table constraints are weak.
Delete/cancel-style operations should default to interactive approval in shared environments.
Per-project quota and allowlisted dataset constraints should be enforced in host policy objects.

notes: Canceling jobs can terminate active workloads and should require explicit user confirmation.
Enforce dataset/project allowlists and per-query cost budgets in host policy.
Read/list/get job operations are generally non-destructive and can stay non-interactive.
Streaming inserts mutate analytic datasets and should be policy-gated.
Permanent table deletion is destructive and requires interactive approval.
Dataset deletion is irreversible for many workflows and should be treated as destructive.
Fail closed for unmapped methods until explicit policy classification is added.

exceptions: Recurring-event and timezone semantics remain service-owned logic and are not fully derivable from Discovery alone.
Cross-calendar ACL mutations can change data visibility and should stay policy-gated even when APIs appear routine.

notes: Deleting events is user-visible data loss and should require explicit approval.
Fail closed for unmapped methods until explicit policy classification is added.

exceptions: Admin Reports is domain-wide and admin-only; the connector must keep tenant and delegated-admin assumptions explicit.
Audit and usage scopes are separate restricted surfaces and should not be silently bundled.

notes: Domain-wide audit logs are read-only but sensitive enough that host policy should approve and zone the call explicitly.
User usage reports expose organization-level productivity telemetry and should stay outside the default audit-only posture.
Customer-wide usage reports summarize domain activity and should remain explicitly policy-gated.
Entity usage reports are niche but still admin-only telemetry and should fail closed without explicit policy mapping.
Fail closed for unmapped methods until explicit policy classification is added.

exceptions: Model invocation itself is usually side-effect free, but downstream tool-use chains can become side-effecting and must be controlled at the host level.
When using API keys rather than OAuth, required_scopes may be empty while policy gating still applies.

notes: Keep host-side prompt provenance and outbound tool policy checks enabled for generated actions.
Streaming output still requires host-level policy for downstream actions.
Fail closed for unmapped methods until explicit policy classification is added.

exceptions: history.list semantics and cursor/lease progression are service-owned and must not be flattened into generic write rules.
Settings and forwarding-related mutations can have high external impact even when method names look routine.

notes: Permanent delete should always require interactive confirmation.
Outbound mail should default to interactive approval to prevent accidental/exfiltrating sends.
Forwarding/filter settings can materially affect data routing and should be policy-gated.
Sync-history cursor progression is a service-owned semantic layer above this mapping.
Fail closed for unmapped methods until explicit policy classification is added.

exceptions: People field masks materially change the sensitivity of returned data and must stay explicit in connector UX rather than hidden behind broad defaults.
Self-profile reads (`people/me`) can require additional personal-profile scopes beyond contacts.readonly and should remain an explicit separate choice.

notes: Permanent contact deletion is user-visible data loss and should require explicit confirmation.
Bulk contact deletion should never ride on the default read-only posture.
Contact creation writes durable personal data and should stay outside the default read-only path.
Contact updates should keep field-mask changes explicit so the caller knows which personal fields are being mutated.
Photo updates still mutate durable personal profile data.

Directory lookups expose org-wide profile data rather than just the user's contacts.

Channel-management mutations can be externally visible and should not default to auto-approval.
